note:
Fallback fill for every ad slot. Instead of an ad-network tag, each slot promotes a project listed in projects.json. The link is built by getReferralUrl(): it uses the code in affiliates.json once you fill it in, otherwise it falls back to the project's plain website URL — so filling in an affiliate code automatically turns that slot into an earning link. Priority is: ads.json (direct-sold) > this file's 'html' (a real Coinzilla/Bitmedia tag, if you add one later) > this file's promo > 'Your Ad Here' placeholder.

RULE: every projectId below must exist as a key in affiliates.json. A project that isn't in that file (Trezor, CoinMarketCap, DexScreener, Magic Eden — all four were here until 2026-09-06) renders a plain link to someone else's site and earns nothing, no matter what you later fill in. It looks identical to a working slot, which is what makes it expensive: those four were quietly eating 24 of 129 ad renders. Check with: node -e "const a=require('./src/data/affiliates.json').exchanges, n=require('./src/data/ad-network.json').slots; for (const [s,v] of Object.entries(n)) console.log(s, v.projectId, v.projectId in a ? 'ok' : 'NEVER EARNS')"

The 8 slots currently map to the 8 exchanges in affiliates.json, one each, so every slot has a path to revenue and no exchange is promoted twice. If you add a 9th exchange, prefer splitting an existing slot's weight over promoting the same brand in two places.
